title: Blind historical backtest of decision-centric versus supply-first research workflows
hypothesis: A decision-centric workflow that begins from an explicit decision, alternatives, affected groups, decision-changing evidence thresholds, predictions, and uncertainty will surface more decision-relevant evidence gaps and produce better-calibrated recommendations than HumanityAI's current supply-first problem/evidence workflow on the same historical cases.
broken_assumption: Architecture ideas should be adopted because they sound conceptually better. Instead, competing HumanityAI workflows should be experimentally compared before structural adoption.

design.case_selection: Choose historical public-interest decisions with a clear information cutoff date, multiple plausible alternatives, publicly available pre-cutoff evidence, and later observable outcomes. Avoid cases already deeply represented in HumanityAI to reduce contamination.
design.blinding: For each case, hide post-cutoff evidence and outcomes from both workflow arms until recommendations and predictions are frozen.
design.arm_a_current_workflow: Use the existing problem-map/evidence/resource/task approach without adding a decision-lifecycle object.
design.arm_b_decision_centric: Represent the concrete decision, alternatives, affected groups, rights/distribution constraints, evidence that would change the choice, key uncertainties, explicit forecasts, and recommended action before gathering targeted evidence.
design.independence: Use separate agent contexts for the two arms when practical. Neither arm should see the other's draft before freeze.
design.freeze: Persist each arm's recommendation, confidence, forecasts, cited evidence, unresolved uncertainties, and rationale before revealing post-cutoff outcomes.
design.evaluation: After freeze, reveal later evidence/outcomes and compare arms using a predeclared rubric. Do not rewrite frozen recommendations after outcome reveal.

primary_measures: decision-relevant evidence gaps identified before outcome reveal
number and importance of assumptions made explicit
forecast calibration against later observable outcomes where measurable
reviewer-rated usefulness for making the historical decision using only pre-cutoff information
guardrails: No consequential real-world action is taken; this is retrospective analysis only.
Do not use post-cutoff information during recommendation generation.
Do not select cases because one workflow is expected to win.
Do not collapse all outcomes into one scalar score; preserve dimensions and reviewer disagreement.
Historical outcome quality is not treated as perfect evidence that the original decision was right or wrong because confounding and stochasticity remain.
Record null or negative results even if the decision-centric workflow does not outperform.
success_condition: Retain or expand the decision-centric architecture only if it repeatedly surfaces materially useful information, uncertainty, or calibration improvements that the current workflow misses at acceptable additional review cost.
failure_condition: If the decision-centric arm mainly adds documentation burden, hindsight-sensitive framing, or no material decision advantage, do not promote it into core architecture without a new hypothesis.
reversibility: High. This experiment adds only a retrospective test specification and does not alter protected governance, security, or core schemas.
next_step: Select three candidate historical cases and preregister their information cutoff dates and evaluation rubric before either workflow analyzes them.
